record.paper_title: Some open problems related to small divisors
record.original_question: Does there exist a C^3 area-preserving twist map of the annulus with a rotational invariant curve of irrational rotation number that is not topologically transitive? Is the answer the same for every r≥3, or even in the analytic category?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1.3 (J. Mather) Does there exist a C3 area-preserving twist map 01 the annulus with a rotational, not topologically transitive, invariant curve 01 irrational rotation number? Same problem with r ~ 3 or even ana­ lytic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A=\mathbb{T}\times[0,1]$ (or $A=\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}$) be the closed (or infinite) annulus, with universal cover $\widetilde A=\mathbb{R}\times[0,1]$. A diffeomorphism $f:A\to A$ is called an area-preserving twist map if it preserves Lebesgue area, preserves boundary components, and a lift $\widetilde f(x,y)=(X(x,y),Y(x,y))$ to $\widetilde A$ satisfies the twist condition $\partial X/\partial y>0$. A rotational invariant curve for $f$ is an essential simple closed curve $\Gamma\subset A$ (i.e., homotopic to $\mathbb{T}\times\{0\}$) with $f(\Gamma)=\Gamma$; by Birkhoff such a $\Gamma$ is the graph of a Lipschitz function. The rotation number of $f|_\Gamma$ is the Poincaré rotation number of the induced circle homeomorphism. The map $f|_\Gamma$ is topologically transitive if it has a dense orbit in $\Gamma$.

Question: Does there exist a $C^3$ area-preserving twist map of the annulus possessing a rotational invariant curve with irrational rotation number on which the restriction of $f$ is not topologically transitive (equivalently, by Denjoy-type considerations, on which $f$ is conjugate to a Denjoy counterexample rather than to an irrational rotation)? Furthermore, does the same hold for every regularity class $C^r$ with $r\ge 3$, and even in the real-analytic category?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active research on regularity and dynamics of irrational invariant curves of twist maps (e.g. Arnaud's non-hyperbolicity results, Fayad–others on non-differentiable irrational curves for $C^1$ twist maps), but no source found that resolves Mather's question of producing a $C^3$ (or higher, or analytic) area-preserving twist map with a non-topologically-transitive rotational invariant curve of irrational rotation number. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Non-differentiable irrational curves for C^1 twist map
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a C^1 symplectic twist map with an essential invariant curve that is not differentiable and on which the map is minimal — addressing only the C^1 (not C^3) regularity case.
status_evidence.claim: Existing constructions of unusual invariant curves are limited to C^1 regularity; the C^3 / analytic case of Mather's question is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: The non-hyperbolicity of irrational invariant curves for twist maps
status_evidence.snippet: Studies regularity (C^1 a.e.) of invariant curves with irrational rotation number for C^{1+alpha} symplectic twist maps.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results focus on regularity rather than constructing non-transitive examples in higher regularity.

status_evidence.title: On Non-KAM Invariant Circles for Area-Preserving Twist Maps
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work providing evidence supporting affirmative answers to Mather's 1998 questions about smooth area-preserving twist maps with invariant curves of irrational rotation number.
status_evidence.claim: Mather's questions in this area are still being actively investigated, indicating the problem is not settled.
